summary: This work presents a fully integrated, open-source quantum error correction (QEC) system built on RISC-Q and implemented on AMD ZCU216 RFSoCs, combining distributed multi-core qubit control, fiber-optic networking, and hardware-accelerated decoding. The system achieves measured end-to-end decoding-feedback latency of 446 ns for a distance-3 surface code and extrapolates to sub-microsecond latency up to distance-21 surface codes (~881 physical qubits).
motivation: While QEC is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computation, prior work has focused primarily on decoder design in isolation, leaving the integration of control, communication, and decoding subsystems as an open engineering challenge. Achieving sub-microsecond feedback latency comparable to Google's 1.1 µs QEC cycle time while scaling to hundreds of qubits requires holistic system design.
method: The system employs a hierarchical architecture with dedicated RISC-V cores (500 MHz) per qubit on leaf nodes, centralized Helios decoder at the root, fiber-optic tree-topology networking using custom 64B/66B protocols achieving 156 ns one-way latency, and sub-nanosecond synchronization via lightweight Precision Time Protocol. All components integrate in hardware on FPGAs with deterministic real-time execution, eliminating software overhead.
result: Measured end-to-end decoding-feedback latency is 446 ns for distance-3 surface code (206 ns aggregation + 56 ns decode + 189 ns error distribution); extrapolation predicts 881 ns latency at distance-21 with one router layer and 476+ qubits, maintaining sub-microsecond performance while achieving 38.26 Gb/s decoder throughput sufficient for 1 µs QEC cycles.
